e-7212.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Union
e-7212.problem: If $\overline{X} = \{ a, c, d\}$ and $\overline{Y} = \{ a, e, i, o, u \},$ then what is $\overline{ X \cup Y }?$
e-7212.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for unions states that

$$
\overline{X \cup Y} \equiv \overline{X} \cap \overline{Y}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X\cup Y} & =\overset{―}{X}\cap \overset{―}{Y} \\  & ={a,c,d}\cap {a,e,i,o,u} \\  & ={a}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7213.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of an Intersection
e-7213.problem: If $\overline{P} = \{ 2, 4, 6 \}$ and $\overline{Q} = \{ 1, 2, 4 \},$ then what is $\overline{ P \cap Q }?$
e-7213.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for intersections states that

$$
\overline{P \cap Q} \equiv \overline{P} \cup \overline{Q}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{P\cap Q} & =\overset{―}{P}\cup \overset{―}{Q} \\  & ={2,4,6}\cup {1,2,4} \\  & ={1,2,4,6}.\end{aligned}
$$
